newsitem.title: USA: Commercial Federal to buy Iowa bank.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Federal to buy Iowa bank.

text.p: Commercial Federal Corp said Monday it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Liberty Financial Corp, an Iowa-based, privately held commercial bank and thrift holding company.

Under the agreement, Commercial Federal will acquire through a tax-free reorganization all 8,748,500 of the outstanding shares of Liberty's common stock. Liberty shareholders are to receive 0.306 shares of Commercial Federal's common stock for each share of Liberty common stock.
Based on Commercial Federal's closing stock price on August 15, the transaction has an aggregate value of $108.6 million or $12.41 a share.
Liberty operates seven bank subsidiaries and one thrift subsidiary with 36 branch locations in Iowa and six branch locations in the Tucson, Ariz., metropolitan area.
After the acquisition, Commercial Federal plans to merge the Liberty banks into Commercial Federal Bank, its wholly owned subsidiary.
Liberty has assets of about $620.5 million.
"This acquisition expands our Iowa presence and moves us into an exciting Arizona market," William Fitzgerald, chairman, said in a statement.
This acquisition, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, is subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. It is expected to close during the first quarter of 1998.
Commercial Federal has assets of about $7.1 billion.
